title: autotune: cost-optimization defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost across common workloads by automatically choosing safe defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles, and by exposing a unit-economics tool that lets SREs and customers evaluate cost/latency tradeoffs. This PR implements: 1) an Autotune controller that suggests/sets conservative batching and caching defaults per model/route based on historical p50/p95 latency and seq-length distributions; 2) first-class quantization profile support in the model catalog + compatibility checks (fp16/int8 heuristics + fallback rules); 3) a unit-economics CLI and server-side metric exporter that computes per-request cost estimates using runtime telemetry and kernel-level token accounting. Summary of changes and rationale are below; see linked Linear tickets for experiments and benchmarks. Checklist: - [x] Add controller and DB schema for autosuggestions - [x] Add heuristics for safe batching thresholds and cache TTLs - [x] [x] Integrate quantization profiles into model manifest and startup validation - [x] Add unit-econ service and CLI (offline sim + live estimator) - [x] Add e2e tests and perf benchmarks (canary) - [x] Docs + console UI changes for suggested defaults - [x] Rollout plan: opt-in canary (10% routes) -> gradual rollout with automatic rollback on error rate increase Known limitations: heuristics are conservative (may under-batch for low-latency routes), INT8 profiles require model-specific validation and are opt-in until more coverage is collected. Related: ENG-4213 (autotune controller), ENG-4278 (unit-econ tooling); SUP-312 for customer request.
commits: 3 commits: 1) add autotune controller + DB migration (controller, models, tests); 2) quant profiles + model manifest changes + validation; 3) unit-econ service, CLI, exporter, and console wiring. Commit messages include short benchmarks and pointers to perf scripts.

release_notes: Automated cost-optimization defaults: autotune controller suggests batching/caching defaults per route, quantization profiles are now first-class in the model catalog, and a unit-economics tool (CLI + exporter) provides per-request cost estimates. Rollout: opt-in canary followed by progressive rollout. No breaking API changes.
post_merge_actions: 1) Monitor canary for 72h p95 latency and error-rate; 2) run weekly sampling job to validate quant profile accuracy; 3) update public docs and changelog; 4) schedule post-rollout review with SRE and Customer Success.
benchmark_summary: Canary on standard chat workload: 12-18% token cost reduction on medium-cost routes (3-8 tokens/req) with p95 latency within SLA (+5ms median change). INT8 profiles gave further 6-9% reduction on compatible models with conservative fallback engaged for ~8% of runs.
migration_notes: No schema-breaking changes. DB migration adds suggestions table which is backfillable; controllers default to 'suggest' mode until explicitly applied. Operators can opt-out per-route via route annotation. Quant profiles are opt-in unless admin flips the global allowlist.
rollback_plan: Rollbacks supported via feature-flag and canary controller: flip autotune.enable=false to stop suggestions and revert applied defaults. Quant profile changes are reversible by demoting profiles in the catalog. Unit-econ exporter can be disabled via config flag.
testing_instructions: Run ./ci/perf/canary_benchmarks.yml with sample workload; run tools/unit_econ/cli.py simulate --input tests/fixtures/seq_dist.json; test quant validation with cargo test --package quantization --test profile_validation. See docs/ops/autotune.md for local dev guide.
